```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

SAShiny lets an **unchanged SAS program** act as the server of a Shiny app. A
sidecar YAML contract declares the program's inputs and outputs. SAShiny
validates the inputs, passes them safely to SAS as macro variables, submits the
program verbatim, and collects the results.

Programs run only on a live, licensed SAS system: **SAS 9.4**, **SAS Viya** or
**SAS OnDemand for Academics (ODA)**. There is no offline mode. You are
responsible for holding a valid licence for the system you connect to.

This vignette does not connect to SAS. Chunks that need SAS are shown but not
evaluated.

## The contract

A SAShiny program is a pair of files:

- `analysis.sas`: your SAS program (never modified).
- `analysis.sashiny.yml`: the contract declaring inputs and outputs.

The package ships a minimal example:

```{r}
library(SAShiny)

path <- system.file("examples", "minimal", "minimal.sashiny.yml", package = "SAShiny")
cat(readLines(path), sep = "\n")
```

## Load and validate

Validation needs no SAS.

```{r}
contract <- sas_contract(path)
length(sas_validate(contract)) # 0 means valid
```

Input values are validated and rendered as SAS macro variables before any SAS
code is submitted:

```{r}
sas_render_values(contract$data, list(n_rows = 3))$macros
sas_render_values(contract$data, list(n_rows = 50))$issues[[1]]$code
```

You can also inspect the exact SAS code that would be submitted:

```{r}
macros <- sas_render_values(contract$data, list(n_rows = 3))$macros
program_path <- system.file("examples", "minimal", "minimal.sas", package = "SAShiny")
program <- readBin(program_path, "raw", n = file.info(program_path)$size)
cat(sas_wrapper_code(contract$data, macros, program))
```

## Connect to SAS

Choose one of the three supported systems. Building an engine does not start a
SAS session:

```{r}
engine <- sas_connect("oda", region = "us1")
engine$backend
```

Credentials come from `~/.authinfo` (or, on Posit Connect, the environment
variables `SASHINY_SAS_USER` and `SASHINY_SAS_PASSWORD`). A run also needs your
licence acknowledgement. Without it, nothing is sent to SAS:

```{r}
engine <- sas_connect("oda", region = "us1", license_ack = FALSE)
result <- sas_run(contract, engine, list(n_rows = 3))
result$status
result$metadata$engine_error
```

With a licensed system:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
options(SAShiny.license_ack = TRUE) # I hold a valid licence for this system
engine <- sas_connect("viya", url = "https://viya.example.com")
result <- sas_run(contract, engine, list(n_rows = 3))
result$status
sas_close(engine)
```

## Build and publish an app

```{r, eval = FALSE}
pool <- sas_pool(function() sas_connect("sas94", host = "sas.example.com"), max_size = 4L)
app <- sas_app(list(path), pool, publish = TRUE)
shiny::runApp(app)
```

To deploy to Posit Connect, call `sas_publish()` or use the
*Publish SAShiny app to Posit Connect* addin. Credential files such as
`.authinfo` are never bundled.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
sas_publish("my-app", title = "Class listing", license_ack = TRUE)
```
